title: Twenty Years with Diabetes

patient.name: Mr Krishnan s/o Subramaniam
patient.presenting_complaint: Referred from polyclinic for annual diabetic retinopathy screening — has not had an eye check in 3 years

history.hpc: Mr Krishnan has Type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed 20 years ago. He was referred by his polyclinic for diabetic eye screening, as his last eye check was 3 years ago and was reportedly 'normal'. He has no specific eye complaints today — no pain, no redness, no sudden vision changes. However, he mentions his distance vision has been 'a bit blur' for driving over the past year, and he has occasional tingling in his feet. He has missed several diabetes follow-up appointments due to work commitments as a long-haul lorry driver.
history.pmhx: Type 2 diabetes mellitus for 20 years (last HbA1c 9.1%, done 8 months ago — poorly controlled). Hypertension for 10 years. Hyperlipidaemia. No previous eye surgery or laser treatment. No known kidney disease, but has not had recent renal function tests.
history.family_hx: Both parents had diabetes. One brother had diabetic retinopathy requiring laser treatment.
history.social_hx: Long-haul lorry driver — relies on his vocational driving licence for his livelihood. Smokes about 10 cigarettes a day for 30 years. Drinks alcohol socially. Often skips meals due to irregular driving schedule, which affects blood sugar control.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Normal bilaterally. Mild early cataract changes noted in both lenses.
examination_findings.fundus: To be assessed via dilated examination/retinal photography — not yet performed; patient's last screening was 3 years ago and showed no retinopathy at that time

investigations.va_distance: RE: LogMAR 0.3 (6/12). LE: LogMAR 0.2 (6/9.5). Both reduced from presumed previous normal — relevant given his vocational driving requirements.
investigations.iop_nct: RE: 16 mmHg. LE: 17 mmHg. Both normal.
investigations.vascular_risk_summary: 20-year history of T2DM with poor control (HbA1c 9.1%), hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, smoking, family history of diabetic retinopathy, peripheral neuropathy symptoms (foot tingling), and 3-year gap since last eye screening — multiple compounding risk factors for diabetic retinopathy

diagnosis: High-risk patient for diabetic retinopathy — long duration of poorly controlled diabetes, multiple vascular risk factors, overdue for screening, with new mild reduction in distance VA relevant to his vocational driving licence. Requires comprehensive dilated fundus examination/retinal photography today.

immediate: Conduct a structured history covering: duration of diabetes, most recent HbA1c, other vascular risk factors (hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, smoking), and time since last eye screening
Specifically ask about new visual symptoms, even subtle ones (gradual blurring relevant to driving)
Ask about systemic symptoms suggestive of other diabetic complications (e.g. peripheral neuropathy — tingling feet, nephropathy)
Document all current medications, including aspirin (relevant if any future intervention needed) and diabetes medications
Record family history of diabetic retinopathy
Measure VA and IOP and document accurately, noting the reduction in VA compared to expected normal
Flag this patient as high priority for dilated fundus examination/retinal photography today, given the 3-year screening gap and poor glycaemic control
Note the occupational relevance (vocational driving licence) when documenting visual findings for the doctor
follow_up: Doctor to perform dilated fundus examination and grade any diabetic retinopathy present
If retinopathy is found, doctor to advise on referral pathways (e.g. laser, intravitreal injection) and the implications for his vocational licence if relevant
Encourage patient to re-engage with his diabetes care team to address poor glycaemic control
Ensure he is scheduled for annual screening going forward, with reminders given his history of missed appointments
patient_education: Explain that diabetic eye disease is often silent — the only way to detect it early is through regular screening, especially given his 20-year history and elevated HbA1c
Explain the importance of returning to his diabetes clinic to address his blood sugar control, which directly affects his eye health
Advise him that smoking significantly increases his risk of diabetic eye complications and offer smoking cessation resources/referral
Explain that any change in his vision could affect his vocational driving licence, so he should not skip future eye screening appointments

key_points: Establishes duration of diabetes and most recent HbA1c/glycaemic control
Identifies other vascular risk factors: hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, smoking history
Asks about time since last eye screening and any prior retinopathy/laser treatment
Asks about symptoms of other diabetic complications (e.g. peripheral neuropathy)
Documents family history of diabetic retinopathy and current medications including anticoagulant (aspirin)
Measures VA in both eyes and notes the reduction relevant to his driving occupation
Performs NCT for IOP as part of routine workup
Recognises the need for dilated fundus examination/retinal photography given the screening gap
Documents the vascular risk profile clearly for the doctor
Synthesises the history into a clear high-risk profile for diabetic retinopathy (duration, control, risk factors, screening gap)
Recognises the new VA reduction as clinically relevant, not incidental
Understands the occupational implications (vocational driving licence) of any visual findings
Does not understate the urgency despite the patient having 'no eye complaints'
Prioritises this patient for dilated fundus examination/retinal photography today
Documents the comprehensive vascular and ocular history clearly for doctor handover
Provides patient education connecting systemic glycaemic control to eye health
Addresses modifiable risk factors (smoking) with appropriate referral/advice
Plans for improved follow-up given history of missed appointments
